script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

Title: BLOOM

FADE IN:

INT. BACKYARD - DAY

Four SIBLINGS, ELLA, MAX, ZOE, and OLIVER, aged 20s, sit around a picnic table with their PARENTS, ROB and JESS. The sun filters through the trees as they eat sandwiches and share stories.

ROB
(looks at Ella)
You remember that treehouse we built when you were kids?

ELLA
(smiling)
Yes, Dad. It's where we all spent hours together.

Max, Zoe, and Oliver nod in agreement.

OLIVER
We had some great times in that treehouse.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Ella, Max, and Zoe sit around the kitchen table, each holding a photograph.

ELLA
(examining a photo)
Do you think he'll ever reach out to us?

MAX
(sighs)
I don't know, Ella. It's been five years.

ZOE
(tearfully)
He was a father figure to us. He raised us when Mom left.

Ella and Max nod.

ELLA
But he hurt us, Zoe. We can't just ignore it.

INT. OLIVER'S APARTMENT - DAY

Oliver sits on a couch, looking at a photo of his siblings and their father. He dials a number on his phone and hesitates.

OLIVER
(into the phone)
Dad? It's Oliver. Can we talk?

INT. PARENTS' BEDROOM - NIGHT

Rob and Jess listen to Oliver's voice on the phone.

ROB
(looking at Jess)
We should tell them.

JESS
(sighs)
I know, but it's not easy, Rob.

INT. ELLA'S APARTMENT - DAY

Ella receives a call from Oliver. She looks surprised.

ELLA
(into the phone)
Oliver?

OLIVER
(over the phone)
Can we meet? I have something to tell you.

INT. PARK - DAY

Ella, Max, and Zoe sit on a bench, waiting for Oliver. They look uneasy.

MAX
(whispering to Ella)
What could he want?

ELLA
(shrugs)
I don't know, Max.

Oliver arrives, looking somber.

OLIVER
(sitting down next to them)
I have something to tell you all. Something I've been carrying with me for a long time.

ELLA
(sternly)
Out with it, Oliver.

OLIVER
I made a mistake. I let anger and resentment consume me. I hurt all of you, and for that, I'm truly sorry.

Max, Zoe, and Ella exchange looks of surprise and confusion.

MAX
(angrily)
That's it? An apology?

OLIVER
(nodding)
It's a start. I want to make things right. I want to rebuild our family.

ELLA
(pausing)
We'll consider it. But you need to show us that you mean it.

INT. ROBB'S BAR - NIGHT

The siblings sit around a table, staring at their father, who looks remorseful.

ROB
(looking at his children)
I know I hurt you all. I let my anger and hurt cloud my judgment. I've been living with the weight of my mistakes every day. But I've come to realize that I can't change the past, but I can make amends. I want to be a part of your lives again.

Ella, Max, and Zoe share a look.

ELLA
(looking at her father)
We'll give you a chance, Dad. But you have to prove it to us.

INT. BACKYARD - DAY

The siblings and their father sit around the picnic table, sharing stories and laughing. The sun filters through the trees as they eat sandwiches and enjoy each other's company.

Max, Zoe, and Ella look at their father, who looks happier and more at peace than they've seen him in years.

MAX
(smiling)
It's good to have you back, Dad.

ELLA
(nods)
Yes, it is.

They all share a moment of understanding and forgiveness.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
